I will treat this as a practical setup guide: what Netlify does, how it connects to Git, and the simplest deployment workflow from a Windows machine.

Use Netlify as the “live website host” connected to your Git project.

Simplest workflow

  1. Put your code in a GitHub repository.

  2. Create a Netlify account.

  3. In Netlify, choose Add new project → Import an existing project.

  4. Connect GitHub.

  5. Select your repository.

  6. Set:

Project typeBuild commandPublish directory
Plain HTML/CSS/JSleave blankfolder containing index.html
Vite / Reactnpm run builddist

Netlify deploys the site whenever you push changes to Git. Netlify’s docs confirm that Git-linked sites use continuous deployment and require a build command and publish directory where relevant. Netlify Docs

Your likely setup

If Claude is helping write code locally:

Bash

git commit -m "Update site"
git push

Useful local commands

Install Netlify CLI:

Bash
npm install -g netlify-cli

Login:

Bash
netlify login

Run locally like Netlify:

Bash
netlify dev

Deploy manually:

Bash
netlify deploy

Deploy live:

Bash
netlify deploy --prod

Key concept

Netlify does not replace Git.

Git = version control
GitHub = online code storage
Netlify = turns the code into a live website

For a school/course website, the best workflow is usually:

Local folder → Git commit → GitHub push → Netlify auto-deploys


You said:

treat me as a noob

ChatGPT said:

What Netlify Actually Is

Netlify is a service that puts your website onto the internet.

You build the website on your computer.
Netlify publishes it online.

Think of it like this:

ToolPurpose
GitTracks changes to your code
GitHubStores your code online
NetlifyMakes the website live on the internet

Step 1 — Create a Folder for Your Website

Example:

C:\Users\Richard\Documents\stratos-site

Inside that folder create:

index.html

Example content:

HTML
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <title>Stratos</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Hello World</h1>
</body>
</html>

Save the file.

Step 2 — Open Terminal in That Folder

In Windows:

  • Open the folder

  • Right-click empty space

  • Choose:

    • “Open in Terminal”

    • or “Git Bash Here”

You should now see something like:

Bash
C:\Users\Richard\Documents\stratos-site>

Step 3 — Turn the Folder Into a Git Project

Type:

Bash
git init

This activates Git tracking.

Step 4 — Save the First Version

Type:

Bash
git add .

This tells Git:

“Track all files.”

Then:

Bash
git commit -m "First website version"

This creates a save point.

Step 5 — Create GitHub Account

Go to:

GitHub

Create account.

Step 6 — Create New Repository

Inside GitHub:

  • Press:

    • New Repository

  • Name:

    • stratos-site

  • Leave mostly default

  • Press:

    • Create Repository

GitHub will then show commands.

Step 7 — Connect Your Computer to GitHub

Copy the commands GitHub gives you.

Usually looks like:

Bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/YOURNAME/stratos-site.git
git branch -M main
git push -u origin main

Paste them into terminal.

Now your code exists online.

Step 8 — Create Netlify Account

Go to:

Netlify

Sign in with GitHub.

Step 9 — Put the Website Online

Inside Netlify:

  • “Add new site”

  • “Import existing project”

  • Choose GitHub

  • Choose your repository

Netlify will ask:

SettingValue
Build commandleave blank
Publish directoryleave blank

Then press:

Deploy Site

After ~30 seconds your site is live.

Netlify gives you a random URL like:

amazing-sunflower-123.netlify.app

Step 10 — Update the Website Later

Change your HTML.

Then run:

Bash
git add .
git commit -m "Updated homepage"
git push

Netlify automatically updates the live website.

That is the core workflow forever.

Important Mental Model

You do NOT upload files manually each time.

You:

  1. change files

  2. commit

  3. push

Everything else becomes automatic.

Typical Beginner Mistakes

1. Forgetting to commit

If you only edit files:

  • Git does nothing yet.

You must:

Bash
git commit

2. Forgetting to push

Commit only saves locally.

You must also:

Bash
git push

to send changes online.

3. Wrong publish folder

For plain HTML:

  • leave blank

For React/Vite later:

  • usually dist

Recommended Beginner Stack

Do NOT start with React yet unless necessary.

Start with:

  • HTML

  • CSS

  • small JavaScript

You can build extremely professional sites this way first.

Recommended Tools

ToolRecommendation
Code editorVisual Studio Code
Git GUIGitHub Desktop
HostingNetlify

GitHub Desktop is easier initially than terminal Git.

Simplest Beginner Workflow

First time only

Bash
git init

Every update afterwards

Bash
git add .
git commit -m "Describe changes"
git push

That is the essential loop.

You said:

i note the active web page has an active email. is the email just opening a local email or is the site redirecting?

ChatGPT said:

At the moment, your site is using a mailto: link.

Example from your HTML:

HTML
<a href="mailto:hello@atmosscience.com.au">

That does NOT send email through the website itself.

It simply tells the browser:

“Open the user’s default email application.”

So when clicked:

  • Outlook may open

  • Apple Mail may open

  • Gmail browser compose may open

  • or nothing happens if no email client configured

Important Distinction

Current setup (mailto:)

Website → opens user's email app

No backend.
No server processing.
No form submission.

Real contact form

A real form does:

Website → sends data to server → server emails you

That requires:

  • backend service

  • Netlify Forms

  • Formspree

  • EmailJS

  • custom API

  • etc.

Your Current Site Is NOT Redirecting

It is simply triggering:

mailto:

inside the browser.

So:

  • no redirection

  • no email handling

  • no message storage

Why This Is Fine Initially

For early-stage sites:

  • simple

  • reliable

  • no spam handling

  • no backend setup

Very common for first deployments.

Downsides of mailto:

Some users:

  • do not use local email apps

  • use browser-only Gmail

  • may click and nothing happens

So conversion rate can be lower.

Recommended Next Step Later

Eventually replace with:

  • Netlify Forms

because:

  • extremely easy on Netlify

  • no server coding

  • emails sent automatically

Example Netlify Form

Later your button becomes something like:

HTML
<form name="contact" method="POST" data-netlify="true">

Then:

  • messages arrive in Netlify dashboard

  • optionally forwarded to your email

My Recommendation

Right now:

keep mailto: while learning.

Later:

upgrade to:

  • Netlify Forms
    OR

  • Formspree

once the site structure stabilises.

Important Clarification

Saving the file alone does NOT deploy

This only changes your LOCAL copy.

You must still:

Bash

git commit -m "Updated homepage"
git push

What Triggers Deployment

Deployment happens ONLY after:

Bash
git push

because that updates GitHub.

Netlify watches GitHub for changes.

Typical Workflow In VS Code

1. Edit HTML

3. Push Online

git push

4. Netlify Deploys Automatically

Usually:

  • 10–30 seconds

How To Know Deployment Worked

Inside Netlify:

  • new deploy appears

  • status changes to:

Published

On your computer only.

git push

the live website will NOT change.

A Git repository contains hidden folder:

.git

Your manually created folder does not contain it.
